svg.text: One row per command -- what it does, to the right of its name
Structural commands: the base installs that venvs are built from.
Installs a base CPython interpreter via uv. The first one installed becomes
Lists installed base interpreters, the real versioned target each points to,
which is default, and flags any broken alias.
Deletes a base Python -- and every venv built from it, since a venv can't
outlive the interpreter it was created against.
The day-to-day family: creating and switching environments, and installing packages into them.
Creates a venv from a base interpreter and installs the default package set
Lists every venv, its Python version, and which one is active.
Activates a venv in the current shell.
Deactivates whatever venv is active in the current shell.
Runs one command inside a venv without activating anything -- exit code and
Prints a venv's interpreter path, and nothing else.
Shows or sets the venv every new shell auto-activates -- writes default_venv
to settings.json, not to the venv itself.
Turns auto-activation of the default venv on or off -- also just a
Passthrough to `uv pip install`, into the active venv.
Passthrough to `uv pip list` for the active venv.
Passthrough to `uv pip show` -- full detail on one installed package.
Deletes one venv, force-closing anything holding it open first.
Stage packages and tools on a connected machine, to install from later with no network at all.
Downloads a package and its dependencies as .whl files into ./wheelhouse, to
Same as download-whl, reading specifiers from a requirements file.
Resolves a conda-forge tool and its dependencies into a local conda channel
folder -- the download-whl of the conda-forge side.
Cloning, opening, and installing dependencies from git repositories.
Clones a git repo into repo/<name> -- bootstraps a portable git on Windows
Lists cloned repos and each one's origin remote.
Changes the current shell's directory into a cloned repo.
Opens a cloned repo in the OS file manager.
Installs a cloned repo's dependencies (editable) into a venv -- the active
one by default. Writes into the venv, not the repo.
Installed on demand, portable, and self-contained inside ~/seedling.
Installs a portable VS Code (once) and opens it at a path -- settings,
extensions, and workspace state stay inside ~/seedling.
Opens a cloned repo in VS Code, installing VS Code first if needed.
Underneath it's `tool-install spyder` -- installs into extensions/apps/ with
a PATH launcher, then points it at a venv and seeds
Opens a cloned repo as a Spyder project -- same install-if-needed shape as
Run, not imported -- each installed into its own isolated environment.
Installs a PyPI application (Spyder, JupyterLab, httpie) into its own venv
under extensions/apps/, launchers on PATH -- not your project venv.
Lists installed applications and their versions.
Removes an application's environment and launchers -- leaves whatever it
installed into your project venvs alone.
The non-Python tools -- ripgrep, pandoc, ffmpeg, gh, compilers.
Runs an installed conda-forge tool by its exact path -- works immediately,
no PATH or fresh terminal needed.
Installs a command-line tool from conda-forge via micromamba, plus PATH
Lists installed conda-forge tools and the command(s) each provides.
Removes a conda-forge tool: its environment, launchers, and record.
An organization's own verbs, added to seed.
Runs one [[command]] entry from custom-commands.toml: a fixed argv (run =
[...]), or a script that chains seed subcommands together. No name lists
Force-closes stuck processes -- scoped to seedling by default; --system or a
name widens it to the whole machine.
Updates seed itself from its recorded source, and reports any seedling.conf
drift since install -- never touches venvs, packages, or repos.
Deletes ~/seedling entirely -- keeps the shell hook.
Everything remove-user does, plus removes the shell hook itself -- seed
Purge, then reinstalls from the recorded source -- cloned repos are always
Read-only status, plus applying a fleet-wide deployment profile.
Prints the version of seed that's actually running.
One read-only screen of everything installed: interpreters, venvs, repos,
Verifies every moving part, one line per check -- exits 1 if anything
Renders every logged command into a self-contained, searchable HTML page.
Brings this machine in line with a deployment profile, idempotently -- never
destroys an existing venv or repo.
Views and changes seedling's own settings (default_venv, package_index,
The machine-facing surface -- Makefiles, CI steps, and AI agents -- as capabilities, not new commands.
Reachable without the shell hook -- works in a fresh, non-interactive
process that never loads a shell profile.
Get an interpreter path, or run one command inside a venv, without
summary, venv-list, python-list, which, health-check, package-list -- all
Never blocks on a prompt -- aborts instead, or pre-answers it.
SEEDLING_NONINTERACTIVE=1 / SEEDLING_YES=1 set both for a session.
install/uninstall/venv/remove-venv take an exclusive lock, so parallel CI
jobs or agents queue instead of corrupting site-packages.
Declarative setup: a deployment profile reaches its target state
idempotently -- first provisioning and drift repair, same primitive.
0 success, 1 failure, 127 command not in the venv, 130 interrupt.
